newsitem.title: UK: UK shares firm buy off highs amid election torpor.
newsitem.headline: UK shares firm buy off highs amid election torpor.

text.p: UK shares were firm but off their earlier highs by late morning on Thursday amid directionless election-day trade and with many European centres closed for May day.

The FTSE 100 index was up 2.2 points at 4,438.2 by 1022 GMT, with gainers in a near three-to-two majority. Insurers rose as investment funds upped weightings in the sector but Shell drifted lower as first-quarter results disappointed.
Dealers said another strong performance on Wall Street was finding little response in London, with investors hanging back until the result of the election was known.

With the opposition Labour party holding its strong opinion poll lead, speculation has centred on the size of the party's majority. Some traders have argued that Friday could see a post-election "relief rally," unless the result was a hung parliament.
Yet other participants said confirmation of a big Labour win could just as easily send the market lower, especially with the FTSE 100 trading at near record levels.

"If the screens greet the result by turning blue (indicating rising prices) then it will be reversed," said the head equity trader at one brokerage. "There could be an emergency budget and rates could be raised by a quarter or half percent."
Assuming no major move on Wall Street on Friday, he said, the FTSE 100 could welcome a Labour victory with a decline of between 50 and 60 points.

Trading volume reached a moderate 337 million shares by 1106 GMT. The second-line FTSE 250 index was down 0.4 points at 4,498.3 and the Reuters-HSBC index of the top 150 stocks was up 0.30 points at 1,190.53.

Insurance stocks helped boost the FTSE 100 to a day's high of 4,454.4 in early trade, just short of its record 4,466.5 set on April 30, with Legal & General up 12-1/2p at 426 and Commercial Union up 11-1/2p at 694.
Dealers said funds continued to pump cash into insurers anticipating the sector's increased size or weighting when mutually-owned Norwich Union floats in June.

Reuters was among the day's biggest gainers as the company's co-broker ABN AMRO Hoare Govett issued a positive comment on the stock following upbeat briefings by the company to analysts in New York. Reuters shares wre up 18-1/2p at 653.
Glaxo was down 17-1/2p at 11.96 stg amid profit-taking after the drug stock's advance to record highs, while British Steel was down 4-3/4p at 137-3/4 after a decline in its ADRs in New York.
Shell Transport & Trading was down 6-1/2p at 10.83-1/2 after first-quarter results fell short of some expectations.

Biotechnology company Celltech gained 30p to 595 following a report that German partner Bayer AG said a drug still under test will be launched next year, though analysts described the reports as "wishful thinking."
Utility Cable fell 4-1/2p to 13-1/4 after a profit warning.
Meanwhile, investors were awaiting the next batch of U.S. economic reports after a week of conflicting data on the state of the world's biggest economy.

"The numbers are telling us quite different things about the state of the U.S. economy, so prior to those we'll see some nervousness creep in," a dealer said. The Dow dropped at the start on Wednesday but recovered to end 47 points higher at its first close above 7,000 in seven weeks.
Wednesday's 5.6 percent first-quarter economic growth proved a short-lived influence ahead of the week's key figure, Friday's closely-watched April U.S. employment report.
Gilts were firm but were little affected by an in-line UK purchasing managers report for March, showing manufacturing expanding for the 11th consecutive month.
-- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367
